These three categories are the categories of this community, and they are the ones entitled to the fay' (booty acquired without battle, whose disbursement is directed toward the interests of Islam). These are its people, the ones who are truly its people. May God make us among them by His grace and generosity.

{11} Then God marvelled at the condition of the hypocrites, who gave their brothers among the People of the Book hope of their support and alliance against the believers, saying to them: ﴿If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, ever﴾; that is, we will not obey, in refusing to support you, anyone who blames us or threatens us. ﴿And if you are fought, we will surely support you﴾. ﴿And God testifies that they are liars﴾ in this promise with which they deceived their brothers. This is not surprising for them, for lying is their attribute, deception and delusion are their companions, and hypocrisy and cowardice accompany them.

{12} For this reason God denied them by His saying, whose report was fulfilled as He stated and occurred exactly as He said: ﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them﴾; that is, from their homes in exile and banishment, ﴿due to their love of homeland and their lack of patience in fighting and their failure to fulfil the promise﴾. ﴿And if they are fought, they will not support them﴾; rather, cowardice will overcome them, failure will possess them, and they will forsake their brothers when they most need them. ﴿And if they support them﴾, on assumption and supposition, ﴿they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped﴾; that is, retreat from fighting and support will surely take place from them, and they will not obtain victory from God.

{13} The reason that moved them to this is that you, O believers, ﴿are more fearful in their breasts than God﴾. They feared you more than they fear God, and preferred fear of a creature who possesses for himself and others neither benefit nor harm, over fear of the Creator in whose hand are harm, benefit, giving and withholding. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾, the ranks of matters, nor do they know the realities of things, nor do they consider consequences. Understanding in its entirety is only that the fear, hope and love of the Creator take precedence over all else, and all else follows it.

{14} ﴿They will not fight you all together﴾; that is, while they are gathered, ﴿except within fortified towns or from behind walls﴾; that is, they do not stand firm in fighting you nor resolve upon it, except when they are fortified in towns or behind walls and ramparts. For in that case, they may refuse, relying on their fortresses and walls rather than on their own courage, and this is among the greatest of censures. ﴿Their violence among themselves is severe﴾; that is, their violence among themselves is severe, with no defect in their bodies or their strength. The defect lies only in the weakness of their faith and the lack of unity of their word. For this reason He said: ﴿You think them united﴾ when you see them gathered and supporting one another, ﴿but their hearts are divided﴾; that is, mutually hateful, scattered and dispersed. ﴿That is because﴾ of what requires their attribution of what was mentioned: ﴿they are a people who do not reason﴾; that is, they have no intellect and no sound judgement. For if they had intellects, they would have preferred the superior to the inferior, and would not have accepted for themselves the basest of the two options, and their word would have been united and their hearts harmonious. Thereby they would support one another, assist one another and cooperate in their religious and worldly interests [and benefits]. Such are these forsaken People of the Book, whom God gave victory over through His Messenger, made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, and failed to support those He had promised to aid them.

{15} ﴿Like those who were before them shortly﴾: they are the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿whom Satan adorned their deeds for, and said: "No one among mankind will overcome you today, and I am your protector." But when the two armies sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said: "I am free of you; I see what you do not see!"﴾. Their own selves deceived them, and those who deceived them, who neither benefited them nor warded off punishment from them, until they came to Badr with their pride and self-conceit, supposing that they would attain their hopes against the Messenger of God and the believers. God gave victory to His Messenger and the believers over them. They killed their leaders and chieftains, took prisoners from among them, and those who fled fled. Thereby they tasted the evil consequence of their affair and the outcome of their polytheism and transgression. This is in this world, and ﴿for them﴾ in the Hereafter is ﴿the punishment of the Fire﴾.

{16} The likeness of these hypocrites, who deceived their brothers from the People of the Book, is ﴿like the likeness of Satan when he says to man: "Disbelieve"﴾; that is, he adorned disbelief for him, made it attractive and invited him to it. When he was deceived by it, disbelieved and incurred wretchedness, the Satan who had taken charge of him and invited him to what he invited him to did not benefit him, but disowned him, ﴿and said: "Indeed I am free of you. Indeed I fear God, the Lord of the worlds."﴾; that is, I have no power to ward off the punishment from you, and I will not avail you against the weight of a speck of good.

{17} ﴿So the end of both of them﴾; that is, the caller who is Satan and the one called who is the human, when he obeyed him, ﴿is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein﴾, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed he calls his party only that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾. ﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾, who shared in wrongdoing and disbelief, even if they differ in the severity and intensity of the punishment. This is the practice of Satan with all his allies: he calls them and lures them with deception to what harms them, until when they fall into the snares and the causes of ruin surround them, he disowns them and abandons them. The blame, entirely, falls upon the one who obeyed him, for God has warned against him and admonished, and informed of his aims, his ultimate purpose and his end. So the one who proceeds to obey him is a sinner with full insight, having no excuse.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 59, verse 1–17 (part 1 of 2):

It is a Medinan surah.
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

This surah is called the Surah of Banu al-Nadir (Banu al-Nadir), who were a large group of Jews on the outskirts of Medina at the time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) mission. When the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent and migrated to Medina, they disbelieved in him along with the rest of the Jews who disbelieved. The Prophet (ﷺ) made a truce with the Jewish groups who were his neighbours in Medina. Then, about six months or so after the Battle of Badr, the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to them and asked them to help him pay the blood-money (diyah) for the Banu Kilab whom 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri had killed. They said: "We will do so, O Abu al-Qasim! Sit here until we fulfil your need!" Then some of them withdrew together, and Satan made attractive to them the wretchedness that had been decreed for them, so they conspired to kill him (ﷺ). They said: "Which of you will take this millstone, climb up and drop it on his head to crush him?" Their most wretched man, 'Amr ibn Jihash, said: "I will." Salam ibn Mishkam said to them: "Do not do it; by God, he will certainly be informed of what you have intended, and it would be a breach of the covenant between us and him."

Revelation came to him immediately from his Lord about what they had planned, so he rose quickly and headed for Medina, and his companions followed him. They said: "You rose and we did not notice you!" He informed them of what the Jews had planned. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to them: "Leave Medina and do not live alongside me in it. I have given you a term of ten days; whoever is found after that, I will strike his neck." They stayed for some days preparing for departure. The hypocrite 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent to them: "Do not leave your homes, for I have two thousand men who will enter your fortress with you and die defending you, and Quraydah and your allies from Ghatafan will support you." Their leader Huyayy ibn Akhtab was tempted by what he had said, and sent to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saying: "We will not leave our homes; do what you wish!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions said "Allahu akbar" and rose against them, with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib carrying the banner. They remained in their fortresses, shooting arrows and hurling stones. Quraydah withdrew from them, and Ibn Ubayy and his allies from Ghatafan betrayed them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) besieged them, cut down their palm trees and burned them. They sent to him: "We will leave Medina." He agreed to let them leave with their lives and their children, and that they could take whatever their camels could carry, except weapons. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) seized the wealth and the weapons.

The property of Banu al-Nadir was exclusively for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to meet his needs and the interests of the Muslims, and he did not apply the one-fifth (khums) to it, because God had given it to him as fay' without the Muslims having to charge against it with horses or camels. He expelled them to Khaybar, and among them was Huyayy ibn Akhtab, their chief. He took possession of their land and homes and seized the weapons; they found fifty coats of mail, fifty helmets and three hundred and forty swords. This is the summary of their story as mentioned by the historians of the biographies (ahl al-siyar).

{1} God opens this surah by informing that everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies its Lord, declares Him free of what does not befit His majesty, worships Him and submits to His greatness, because He is the Mighty who has subdued everything, so nothing can defy Him and no difficulty is beyond Him; the Wise in His creation and command, so He creates nothing in vain and legislates nothing devoid of benefit, and does nothing except what His wisdom requires.

{2} Among that is His support of His Messenger (ﷺ) against those among the People of the Book who disbelieved, the Banu al-Nadir, when they betrayed His Messenger, so He expelled them from their homes and homelands which they had grown accustomed to and loved. Their expulsion from there was the first gathering (hashr) and exile (jala') which God had decreed against them through the hand of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so they went to Khaybar. The noble verse indicates that they had another gathering and exile besides this; it occurred when the Prophet (ﷺ) expelled them from Khaybar, and then 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) expelled the rest of them from it. {You did not think} O Muslims {that they would go out} from their homes, because of their fortification, their strength and their honour in them, {and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah}; so they were pleased with them, were deceived by them, and reckoned that they could not be reached and no one could overcome them. But the decree of God is beyond all of that; fortresses and castles avail nothing against it, and strength and defence are of no use against it. Hence He said: {So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect}; that is, from the matter and the direction which had never occurred to them that they could be struck from, namely that He, exalted is He, {cast terror into their hearts}: and this is intense fear, which is the greatest army of Allah, against which no number, equipment, strength or might avails. The thing they counted on, and thought that a breach would enter upon them through it if it came, was the fortresses in which they had fortified themselves and in which their souls were at rest. Whoever trusts in other than God is forsaken, and whoever relies on other than God will be a burden to him. So a heavenly command came upon them, descending upon their hearts, which are the seat of steadfastness and patience or of weakness and feebleness, and it removed their strength and firmness and left them with a weakness, cowardice and fear for which they had no means of repelling. This became a help against them. Hence He said: {They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers}, because they had made peace with the Prophet (ﷺ) on condition that they would have what the camels could carry; so they tore down much of the roofing they had admired, and because of their transgression God gave the believers power to ruin their homes and demolish their fortresses. Thus it was they who brought ruin upon themselves and became the greatest help against themselves. {So take warning, O you with vision}; that is, those with penetrating insight and perfect intellect, for in this there is a lesson by which one recognises the working of God [exalted is He] against those who oppose the truth and follow their desires, those whose might did not benefit them, whose strength did not protect them, and whose fortresses did not shelter them when the command of God came upon them; punishment reached them for their sins. The lesson lies in the generality of the meaning, not the particularity of the cause; this verse indicates the command to take lessons, which is to draw an analogy from one case to its like, and to reason from a thing to what resembles it, and to reflect upon the meanings and wisdoms contained in the rulings, which are the domain of intellect and thought. By this the intellect is perfected, insight is illuminated, faith increases, and true understanding is attained.

{3} Then God informed that these Jews had not received the full punishment they deserved, and that God lightened it for them. Had it not been that He had decreed for them the exile which befell them, and determined it by His decree which is neither changed nor altered, there would have been for them another matter of worldly punishment and chastisement. But although the severe worldly punishment escaped them, they have in the Hereafter the punishment of the Fire, the intensity of which none can know except God. It should not occur to them that their punishment has ended and finished, leaving them no remainder of it; for what God has prepared for them of punishment in the Hereafter is greater and more grievous.

{4} And that is because {they opposed Allah and His Messenger}: they were hostile to them, fought them and strove in disobedience to them, and this is His custom and practice with whoever opposes Him. {And whoever opposes Allah, indeed Allah is severe in penalty}.

{5} When Banu al-Nadir blamed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Muslims for cutting down the palm trees and trees, claiming that this was corruption and using it as a pretext to slander the Muslims, God informed that cutting the palms, whether they cut them or left them standing, was by His permission and command, {and to disgrace the defiantly disobedient}: since He empowered you to cut down and burn their palms, so that this would be a punishment and disgrace for them in this world, and a humiliation by which their complete helplessness would be known, for they could not rescue their palms, which were the source of their sustenance. The word līnah (palm trees) includes all palm trees according to the most correct and preferable interpretation. This is the state of Banu al-Nadir and how God punished them in this world.

{6} Then He mentioned who received their wealth and property, saying: {And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them}; that is, from the people of this town, namely Banu al-Nadir, {for which you did not spur on horse or camel}; that is, you did not urge or muster any effort for it; you did not exert yourselves in obtaining it, neither with your persons nor with your animals. Rather, God cast terror into their hearts, and it came to you freely and without struggle. Hence He said: {But Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent}: of the perfection of His power is that none can resist Him and no strong one can be mighty without Him.

{7} The definition of fay' according to the terminology of the jurists is: what is taken from the property of the disbelievers rightfully and without fighting, like this property which they fled and left out of fear of the Muslims. It is called fay' because it returned from the disbelievers, who were not entitled to it, to the Muslims, who have the greatest right to it. Its general ruling is as God mentioned in His words: {What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns}: in general, whether at the time of the Messenger or after him, for those who take charge after him from his community. {Is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer}. This verse is similar to the verse in Surah al-Anfal, His words: {And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, then for Allah is one-fifth of it and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer}. So this fay' is divided into five parts: for Allah and His Messenger, it is spent on the general interests of the Muslims. One-fifth is for the near relatives, who are Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib wherever they are, with males and females treated equally. Banu al-Muttalib were included in the fifth of the fifth along with Banu Hashim, and not the rest of Banu 'Abd Manaf, because they shared with Banu Hashim in entering the shi'b when Quraysh agreed to boycott and oppose them, and they supported the Messenger of God (ﷺ), unlike the others. Hence the Prophet (ﷺ) said of Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib: "They never separated from me in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam." One-fifth is for the poor orphans, who are those without a father who have not reached maturity. One-fifth is for the needy. One-fifth is for the wayfarers, who are strangers cut off from their homelands.

God decreed this apportionment and restricted the fay' to these specified groups so that it would {not be a circulation}; that is, a passing around and exclusive possession {among the rich among you}. For had He not decreed it, the wealthy and powerful would have monopolised it, and none of the weak others would have obtained anything of it, and in that there is corruption that none knows except God. Just as in following God's command and law there are benefits that cannot be counted. For this reason God commanded the universal principle and general foundation, saying: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and what he forbids you, refrain from}. This encompasses the roots and branches of religion, outward and inward, and that what the Messenger brought is binding on the servants to adopt and follow, and it is not permissible to oppose it; the Messenger's ruling on a matter is like God's own text, there is no concession for anyone nor any excuse for abandoning it, and it is not permissible to prefer anyone's word over his. Then He commanded piety, by which the hearts, souls, this world and the Hereafter are cultivated, and by which is lasting happiness and great success, while by neglecting it comes everlasting wretchedness and eternal punishment. He said: {And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty}: upon whoever abandons piety and prefers following desire.

{8–9} Then God mentioned the wisdom and the cause that makes Him assign the wealth of fay' to those for whom He determined it, and that they are deserving of help and entitled to be given it: they are the Muhajirun, who left behind what they loved and were accustomed to, their homes, homelands, beloved ones, friends and wealth, out of desire for God, support for the religion of God and love for the Messenger of God. These are the truthful ones, who acted according to the requirements of their faith and confirmed their faith by righteous deeds and arduous worship. This is unlike one who claims faith but does not confirm it through jihad, emigration and other acts of worship. And there are the Ansar, namely the Aws and the Khazraj, who believed in God and His Messenger willingly, lovingly and by choice, sheltered the Messenger of God (ﷺ), protected him from red and black alike, and took up the abode of emigration and faith, until it became a refuge and a place of return to which the believers turn, where the emigrants seek shelter and the Muslims dwell under its protection, for all other lands were then lands of war, polytheism and evil. The helpers of the religion continued to take refuge with the Ansar until Islam spread, grew strong and kept increasing little by little, [and developing gradually], until they conquered hearts through knowledge, faith and the Qur'an, and lands through the sword and the spear. Among their beautiful qualities is that {they love those who emigrate to them}, and this is due to their love for God and His Messenger: they love His beloved ones and love those who support His religion. {And they find no need in their breasts for what they have been given}; that is, they do not envy the emigrants for what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty and singled them out with of virtues and merits, for they are the people of them.

This indicates the soundness of their hearts and the absence of rancour, hatred and envy from them. It also indicates that the emigrants are superior to the Ansar, because God mentioned them first and informed that the Ansar find in their breasts no need for what they were given, which shows that God gave the emigrants what He did not give the Ansar or anyone else, and because they combined both helping and emigrating. His words: {And they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation}; that is, among the qualities of the Ansar by which they surpassed others and were distinguished from all others is preference (ithar), which is the most perfect kind of generosity: giving away what the self loves, of wealth and other things, to others while still in need of it, indeed even in dire necessity and want. This comes only from a pure character and love for God that takes precedence over the desires and pleasures of the self. Among this is the story of the Ansari whose conduct the verse was revealed about, when he preferred his guest with his food, and the food of his household and children, and they spent the night hungry.

Preference is the opposite of selfishness (athara); preference is praiseworthy, while selfishness is blameworthy, for it is one of the traits of miserliness and avarice. Whoever is granted preference has been guarded from the avarice of his own soul. {And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful}. The protection from the stinginess of the soul includes its protection from stinginess in all that has been commanded, for when a servant is protected from the stinginess of his soul, his soul yields to the commands of God and His Messenger, and he performs them willingly, compliantly, with his chest expanded by them; his soul yields to abandoning what God has forbidden even if it is beloved to the self, which calls to it and longs for it; and his soul yields to spending wealth in the way of God and seeking His pleasure. By this success and victory are attained. This is unlike one who is not protected from the stinginess of his soul, but is afflicted with miserliness regarding good, which is the root and source of evil.

The commentary on verses 1–17 of Surah al-Hashr (part 2 of 2):

{10} These two virtuous and purified groups are the noble Companions and the eminent leaders, who attained such precedence, merits and virtues that they outstripped those after them and attained what those before them had attained. They became the foremost of the believers, the masters of the Muslims and the leaders of the God-fearing. It is enough of a virtue for those who come after them that they follow them and take their guidance as a model. For this reason, God mentioned among the later generations those who follow them, [and the rest of their successors], saying: ﴿And those who came after them﴾; that is, after the Emigrants and the Helpers. ﴿They say﴾, sincerely counselling themselves and all the believers: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾. This is a supplication that encompasses all the believers, from the earlier Companions and those before them and those after them. This is one of the virtues of faith: believers benefit one another and pray for one another, by virtue of their sharing in faith, which necessitates a bond of brotherhood among the believers, one of whose branches is that they pray for one another and love one another. For this reason, God mentioned in this supplication the removal of rancour from the heart, which covers both little and much of it. When it is removed, its opposite is established: love among the believers, loyalty, sincere counsel and the like, which are among the rights of the believers. God described those after the Companions as believers, because their saying ﴿who preceded us in faith﴾ is evidence of their sharing in it, and that they follow the Companions in the creed of faith and its foundations. They are the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah, the adherents of the prophetic way and the united body of the Muslims), and this complete description applies only to them. He described them as acknowledging their sins and seeking forgiveness for them, as seeking forgiveness for one another, and as striving to remove rancour and hatred ﴿from their hearts﴾ toward their believing brothers. Their supplication for this necessitates what we have mentioned, and includes love among them, and that each of them loves for his brother what he loves for himself, and gives him sincere counsel, present or absent, living or dead.
The noble verse indicates that this is among the rights of the believers toward one another. Then they concluded their supplication with two noble names, indicating the perfection of God's mercy and the intensity of His compassion and kindness toward them. Among the greatest of these is His granting them success in fulfilling His rights and the rights of His servants.
These three categories are the categories of this community, and they are the ones entitled to the fay' (booty acquired without battle, whose disbursement is directed toward the interests of Islam). These are its people, the ones who are truly its people. May God make us among them by His grace and generosity.

{11} Then God marvelled at the condition of the hypocrites, who gave their brothers among the People of the Book hope of their support and alliance against the believers, saying to them: ﴿If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, ever﴾; that is, we will not obey, in refusing to support you, anyone who blames us or threatens us. ﴿And if you are fought, we will surely support you﴾. ﴿And God testifies that they are liars﴾ in this promise with which they deceived their brothers. This is not surprising for them, for lying is their attribute, deception and delusion are their companions, and hypocrisy and cowardice accompany them.

{12} For this reason God denied them by His saying, whose report was fulfilled as He stated and occurred exactly as He said: ﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them﴾; that is, from their homes in exile and banishment, ﴿due to their love of homeland and their lack of patience in fighting and their failure to fulfil the promise﴾. ﴿And if they are fought, they will not support them﴾; rather, cowardice will overcome them, failure will possess them, and they will forsake their brothers when they most need them. ﴿And if they support them﴾, on assumption and supposition, ﴿they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped﴾; that is, retreat from fighting and support will surely take place from them, and they will not obtain victory from God.

{13} The reason that moved them to this is that you, O believers, ﴿are more fearful in their breasts than God﴾. They feared you more than they fear God, and preferred fear of a creature who possesses for himself and others neither benefit nor harm, over fear of the Creator in whose hand are harm, benefit, giving and withholding. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾, the ranks of matters, nor do they know the realities of things, nor do they consider consequences. Understanding in its entirety is only that the fear, hope and love of the Creator take precedence over all else, and all else follows it.

{14} ﴿They will not fight you all together﴾; that is, while they are gathered, ﴿except within fortified towns or from behind walls﴾; that is, they do not stand firm in fighting you nor resolve upon it, except when they are fortified in towns or behind walls and ramparts. For in that case, they may refuse, relying on their fortresses and walls rather than on their own courage, and this is among the greatest of censures. ﴿Their violence among themselves is severe﴾; that is, their violence among themselves is severe, with no defect in their bodies or their strength. The defect lies only in the weakness of their faith and the lack of unity of their word. For this reason He said: ﴿You think them united﴾ when you see them gathered and supporting one another, ﴿but their hearts are divided﴾; that is, mutually hateful, scattered and dispersed. ﴿That is because﴾ of what requires their attribution of what was mentioned: ﴿they are a people who do not reason﴾; that is, they have no intellect and no sound judgement. For if they had intellects, they would have preferred the superior to the inferior, and would not have accepted for themselves the basest of the two options, and their word would have been united and their hearts harmonious. Thereby they would support one another, assist one another and cooperate in their religious and worldly interests [and benefits]. Such are these forsaken People of the Book, whom God gave victory over through His Messenger, made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, and failed to support those He had promised to aid them.

{15} ﴿Like those who were before them shortly﴾: they are the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿whom Satan adorned their deeds for, and said: "No one among mankind will overcome you today, and I am your protector." But when the two armies sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said: "I am free of you; I see what you do not see!"﴾. Their own selves deceived them, and those who deceived them, who neither benefited them nor warded off punishment from them, until they came to Badr with their pride and self-conceit, supposing that they would attain their hopes against the Messenger of God and the believers. God gave victory to His Messenger and the believers over them. They killed their leaders and chieftains, took prisoners from among them, and those who fled fled. Thereby they tasted the evil consequence of their affair and the outcome of their polytheism and transgression. This is in this world, and ﴿for them﴾ in the Hereafter is ﴿the punishment of the Fire﴾.

{16} The likeness of these hypocrites, who deceived their brothers from the People of the Book, is ﴿like the likeness of Satan when he says to man: "Disbelieve"﴾; that is, he adorned disbelief for him, made it attractive and invited him to it. When he was deceived by it, disbelieved and incurred wretchedness, the Satan who had taken charge of him and invited him to what he invited him to did not benefit him, but disowned him, ﴿and said: "Indeed I am free of you. Indeed I fear God, the Lord of the worlds."﴾; that is, I have no power to ward off the punishment from you, and I will not avail you against the weight of a speck of good.

{17} ﴿So the end of both of them﴾; that is, the caller who is Satan and the one called who is the human, when he obeyed him, ﴿is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein﴾, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed he calls his party only that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾. ﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾, who shared in wrongdoing and disbelief, even if they differ in the severity and intensity of the punishment. This is the practice of Satan with all his allies: he calls them and lures them with deception to what harms them, until when they fall into the snares and the causes of ruin surround them, he disowns them and abandons them. The blame, entirely, falls upon the one who obeyed him, for God has warned against him and admonished, and informed of his aims, his ultimate purpose and his end. So the one who proceeds to obey him is a sinner with full insight, having no excuse.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 59, verse 1–17 (part 1 of 2):

It is a Medinan surah.
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

This surah is called the Surah of Banu al-Nadir (Banu al-Nadir), who were a large group of Jews on the outskirts of Medina at the time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) mission. When the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent and migrated to Medina, they disbelieved in him along with the rest of the Jews who disbelieved. The Prophet (ﷺ) made a truce with the Jewish groups who were his neighbours in Medina. Then, about six months or so after the Battle of Badr, the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to them and asked them to help him pay the blood-money (diyah) for the Banu Kilab whom 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri had killed. They said: "We will do so, O Abu al-Qasim! Sit here until we fulfil your need!" Then some of them withdrew together, and Satan made attractive to them the wretchedness that had been decreed for them, so they conspired to kill him (ﷺ). They said: "Which of you will take this millstone, climb up and drop it on his head to crush him?" Their most wretched man, 'Amr ibn Jihash, said: "I will." Salam ibn Mishkam said to them: "Do not do it; by God, he will certainly be informed of what you have intended, and it would be a breach of the covenant between us and him."

Revelation came to him immediately from his Lord about what they had planned, so he rose quickly and headed for Medina, and his companions followed him. They said: "You rose and we did not notice you!" He informed them of what the Jews had planned. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to them: "Leave Medina and do not live alongside me in it. I have given you a term of ten days; whoever is found after that, I will strike his neck." They stayed for some days preparing for departure. The hypocrite 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul sent to them: "Do not leave your homes, for I have two thousand men who will enter your fortress with you and die defending you, and Quraydah and your allies from Ghatafan will support you." Their leader Huyayy ibn Akhtab was tempted by what he had said, and sent to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saying: "We will not leave our homes; do what you wish!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions said "Allahu akbar" and rose against them, with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib carrying the banner. They remained in their fortresses, shooting arrows and hurling stones. Quraydah withdrew from them, and Ibn Ubayy and his allies from Ghatafan betrayed them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) besieged them, cut down their palm trees and burned them. They sent to him: "We will leave Medina." He agreed to let them leave with their lives and their children, and that they could take whatever their camels could carry, except weapons. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) seized the wealth and the weapons.

The property of Banu al-Nadir was exclusively for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to meet his needs and the interests of the Muslims, and he did not apply the one-fifth (khums) to it, because God had given it to him as fay' without the Muslims having to charge against it with horses or camels. He expelled them to Khaybar, and among them was Huyayy ibn Akhtab, their chief. He took possession of their land and homes and seized the weapons; they found fifty coats of mail, fifty helmets and three hundred and forty swords. This is the summary of their story as mentioned by the historians of the biographies (ahl al-siyar).

{1} God opens this surah by informing that everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies its Lord, declares Him free of what does not befit His majesty, worships Him and submits to His greatness, because He is the Mighty who has subdued everything, so nothing can defy Him and no difficulty is beyond Him; the Wise in His creation and command, so He creates nothing in vain and legislates nothing devoid of benefit, and does nothing except what His wisdom requires.

{2} Among that is His support of His Messenger (ﷺ) against those among the People of the Book who disbelieved, the Banu al-Nadir, when they betrayed His Messenger, so He expelled them from their homes and homelands which they had grown accustomed to and loved. Their expulsion from there was the first gathering (hashr) and exile (jala') which God had decreed against them through the hand of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so they went to Khaybar. The noble verse indicates that they had another gathering and exile besides this; it occurred when the Prophet (ﷺ) expelled them from Khaybar, and then 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) expelled the rest of them from it. {You did not think} O Muslims {that they would go out} from their homes, because of their fortification, their strength and their honour in them, {and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah}; so they were pleased with them, were deceived by them, and reckoned that they could not be reached and no one could overcome them. But the decree of God is beyond all of that; fortresses and castles avail nothing against it, and strength and defence are of no use against it. Hence He said: {So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect}; that is, from the matter and the direction which had never occurred to them that they could be struck from, namely that He, exalted is He, {cast terror into their hearts}: and this is intense fear, which is the greatest army of Allah, against which no number, equipment, strength or might avails. The thing they counted on, and thought that a breach would enter upon them through it if it came, was the fortresses in which they had fortified themselves and in which their souls were at rest. Whoever trusts in other than God is forsaken, and whoever relies on other than God will be a burden to him. So a heavenly command came upon them, descending upon their hearts, which are the seat of steadfastness and patience or of weakness and feebleness, and it removed their strength and firmness and left them with a weakness, cowardice and fear for which they had no means of repelling. This became a help against them. Hence He said: {They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers}, because they had made peace with the Prophet (ﷺ) on condition that they would have what the camels could carry; so they tore down much of the roofing they had admired, and because of their transgression God gave the believers power to ruin their homes and demolish their fortresses. Thus it was they who brought ruin upon themselves and became the greatest help against themselves. {So take warning, O you with vision}; that is, those with penetrating insight and perfect intellect, for in this there is a lesson by which one recognises the working of God [exalted is He] against those who oppose the truth and follow their desires, those whose might did not benefit them, whose strength did not protect them, and whose fortresses did not shelter them when the command of God came upon them; punishment reached them for their sins. The lesson lies in the generality of the meaning, not the particularity of the cause; this verse indicates the command to take lessons, which is to draw an analogy from one case to its like, and to reason from a thing to what resembles it, and to reflect upon the meanings and wisdoms contained in the rulings, which are the domain of intellect and thought. By this the intellect is perfected, insight is illuminated, faith increases, and true understanding is attained.

{3} Then God informed that these Jews had not received the full punishment they deserved, and that God lightened it for them. Had it not been that He had decreed for them the exile which befell them, and determined it by His decree which is neither changed nor altered, there would have been for them another matter of worldly punishment and chastisement. But although the severe worldly punishment escaped them, they have in the Hereafter the punishment of the Fire, the intensity of which none can know except God. It should not occur to them that their punishment has ended and finished, leaving them no remainder of it; for what God has prepared for them of punishment in the Hereafter is greater and more grievous.

{4} And that is because {they opposed Allah and His Messenger}: they were hostile to them, fought them and strove in disobedience to them, and this is His custom and practice with whoever opposes Him. {And whoever opposes Allah, indeed Allah is severe in penalty}.

{5} When Banu al-Nadir blamed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the Muslims for cutting down the palm trees and trees, claiming that this was corruption and using it as a pretext to slander the Muslims, God informed that cutting the palms, whether they cut them or left them standing, was by His permission and command, {and to disgrace the defiantly disobedient}: since He empowered you to cut down and burn their palms, so that this would be a punishment and disgrace for them in this world, and a humiliation by which their complete helplessness would be known, for they could not rescue their palms, which were the source of their sustenance. The word līnah (palm trees) includes all palm trees according to the most correct and preferable interpretation. This is the state of Banu al-Nadir and how God punished them in this world.

{6} Then He mentioned who received their wealth and property, saying: {And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them}; that is, from the people of this town, namely Banu al-Nadir, {for which you did not spur on horse or camel}; that is, you did not urge or muster any effort for it; you did not exert yourselves in obtaining it, neither with your persons nor with your animals. Rather, God cast terror into their hearts, and it came to you freely and without struggle. Hence He said: {But Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent}: of the perfection of His power is that none can resist Him and no strong one can be mighty without Him.

{7} The definition of fay' according to the terminology of the jurists is: what is taken from the property of the disbelievers rightfully and without fighting, like this property which they fled and left out of fear of the Muslims. It is called fay' because it returned from the disbelievers, who were not entitled to it, to the Muslims, who have the greatest right to it. Its general ruling is as God mentioned in His words: {What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns}: in general, whether at the time of the Messenger or after him, for those who take charge after him from his community. {Is for Allah and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer}. This verse is similar to the verse in Surah al-Anfal, His words: {And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, then for Allah is one-fifth of it and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer}. So this fay' is divided into five parts: for Allah and His Messenger, it is spent on the general interests of the Muslims. One-fifth is for the near relatives, who are Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib wherever they are, with males and females treated equally. Banu al-Muttalib were included in the fifth of the fifth along with Banu Hashim, and not the rest of Banu 'Abd Manaf, because they shared with Banu Hashim in entering the shi'b when Quraysh agreed to boycott and oppose them, and they supported the Messenger of God (ﷺ), unlike the others. Hence the Prophet (ﷺ) said of Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib: "They never separated from me in the Jahiliyyah or in Islam." One-fifth is for the poor orphans, who are those without a father who have not reached maturity. One-fifth is for the needy. One-fifth is for the wayfarers, who are strangers cut off from their homelands.

God decreed this apportionment and restricted the fay' to these specified groups so that it would {not be a circulation}; that is, a passing around and exclusive possession {among the rich among you}. For had He not decreed it, the wealthy and powerful would have monopolised it, and none of the weak others would have obtained anything of it, and in that there is corruption that none knows except God. Just as in following God's command and law there are benefits that cannot be counted. For this reason God commanded the universal principle and general foundation, saying: {And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and what he forbids you, refrain from}. This encompasses the roots and branches of religion, outward and inward, and that what the Messenger brought is binding on the servants to adopt and follow, and it is not permissible to oppose it; the Messenger's ruling on a matter is like God's own text, there is no concession for anyone nor any excuse for abandoning it, and it is not permissible to prefer anyone's word over his. Then He commanded piety, by which the hearts, souls, this world and the Hereafter are cultivated, and by which is lasting happiness and great success, while by neglecting it comes everlasting wretchedness and eternal punishment. He said: {And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty}: upon whoever abandons piety and prefers following desire.

{8–9} Then God mentioned the wisdom and the cause that makes Him assign the wealth of fay' to those for whom He determined it, and that they are deserving of help and entitled to be given it: they are the Muhajirun, who left behind what they loved and were accustomed to, their homes, homelands, beloved ones, friends and wealth, out of desire for God, support for the religion of God and love for the Messenger of God. These are the truthful ones, who acted according to the requirements of their faith and confirmed their faith by righteous deeds and arduous worship. This is unlike one who claims faith but does not confirm it through jihad, emigration and other acts of worship. And there are the Ansar, namely the Aws and the Khazraj, who believed in God and His Messenger willingly, lovingly and by choice, sheltered the Messenger of God (ﷺ), protected him from red and black alike, and took up the abode of emigration and faith, until it became a refuge and a place of return to which the believers turn, where the emigrants seek shelter and the Muslims dwell under its protection, for all other lands were then lands of war, polytheism and evil. The helpers of the religion continued to take refuge with the Ansar until Islam spread, grew strong and kept increasing little by little, [and developing gradually], until they conquered hearts through knowledge, faith and the Qur'an, and lands through the sword and the spear. Among their beautiful qualities is that {they love those who emigrate to them}, and this is due to their love for God and His Messenger: they love His beloved ones and love those who support His religion. {And they find no need in their breasts for what they have been given}; that is, they do not envy the emigrants for what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty and singled them out with of virtues and merits, for they are the people of them.

This indicates the soundness of their hearts and the absence of rancour, hatred and envy from them. It also indicates that the emigrants are superior to the Ansar, because God mentioned them first and informed that the Ansar find in their breasts no need for what they were given, which shows that God gave the emigrants what He did not give the Ansar or anyone else, and because they combined both helping and emigrating. His words: {And they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves were in privation}; that is, among the qualities of the Ansar by which they surpassed others and were distinguished from all others is preference (ithar), which is the most perfect kind of generosity: giving away what the self loves, of wealth and other things, to others while still in need of it, indeed even in dire necessity and want. This comes only from a pure character and love for God that takes precedence over the desires and pleasures of the self. Among this is the story of the Ansari whose conduct the verse was revealed about, when he preferred his guest with his food, and the food of his household and children, and they spent the night hungry.

Preference is the opposite of selfishness (athara); preference is praiseworthy, while selfishness is blameworthy, for it is one of the traits of miserliness and avarice. Whoever is granted preference has been guarded from the avarice of his own soul. {And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful}. The protection from the stinginess of the soul includes its protection from stinginess in all that has been commanded, for when a servant is protected from the stinginess of his soul, his soul yields to the commands of God and His Messenger, and he performs them willingly, compliantly, with his chest expanded by them; his soul yields to abandoning what God has forbidden even if it is beloved to the self, which calls to it and longs for it; and his soul yields to spending wealth in the way of God and seeking His pleasure. By this success and victory are attained. This is unlike one who is not protected from the stinginess of his soul, but is afflicted with miserliness regarding good, which is the root and source of evil.

The commentary on verses 1–17 of Surah al-Hashr (part 2 of 2):

{10} These two virtuous and purified groups are the noble Companions and the eminent leaders, who attained such precedence, merits and virtues that they outstripped those after them and attained what those before them had attained. They became the foremost of the believers, the masters of the Muslims and the leaders of the God-fearing. It is enough of a virtue for those who come after them that they follow them and take their guidance as a model. For this reason, God mentioned among the later generations those who follow them, [and the rest of their successors], saying: ﴿And those who came after them﴾; that is, after the Emigrants and the Helpers. ﴿They say﴾, sincerely counselling themselves and all the believers: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾. This is a supplication that encompasses all the believers, from the earlier Companions and those before them and those after them. This is one of the virtues of faith: believers benefit one another and pray for one another, by virtue of their sharing in faith, which necessitates a bond of brotherhood among the believers, one of whose branches is that they pray for one another and love one another. For this reason, God mentioned in this supplication the removal of rancour from the heart, which covers both little and much of it. When it is removed, its opposite is established: love among the believers, loyalty, sincere counsel and the like, which are among the rights of the believers. God described those after the Companions as believers, because their saying ﴿who preceded us in faith﴾ is evidence of their sharing in it, and that they follow the Companions in the creed of faith and its foundations. They are the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah, the adherents of the prophetic way and the united body of the Muslims), and this complete description applies only to them. He described them as acknowledging their sins and seeking forgiveness for them, as seeking forgiveness for one another, and as striving to remove rancour and hatred ﴿from their hearts﴾ toward their believing brothers. Their supplication for this necessitates what we have mentioned, and includes love among them, and that each of them loves for his brother what he loves for himself, and gives him sincere counsel, present or absent, living or dead.
The noble verse indicates that this is among the rights of the believers toward one another. Then they concluded their supplication with two noble names, indicating the perfection of God's mercy and the intensity of His compassion and kindness toward them. Among the greatest of these is His granting them success in fulfilling His rights and the rights of His servants.
These three categories are the categories of this community, and they are the ones entitled to the fay' (booty acquired without battle, whose disbursement is directed toward the interests of Islam). These are its people, the ones who are truly its people. May God make us among them by His grace and generosity.

{11} Then God marvelled at the condition of the hypocrites, who gave their brothers among the People of the Book hope of their support and alliance against the believers, saying to them: ﴿If you are expelled, we will surely go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, ever﴾; that is, we will not obey, in refusing to support you, anyone who blames us or threatens us. ﴿And if you are fought, we will surely support you﴾. ﴿And God testifies that they are liars﴾ in this promise with which they deceived their brothers. This is not surprising for them, for lying is their attribute, deception and delusion are their companions, and hypocrisy and cowardice accompany them.

{12} For this reason God denied them by His saying, whose report was fulfilled as He stated and occurred exactly as He said: ﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them﴾; that is, from their homes in exile and banishment, ﴿due to their love of homeland and their lack of patience in fighting and their failure to fulfil the promise﴾. ﴿And if they are fought, they will not support them﴾; rather, cowardice will overcome them, failure will possess them, and they will forsake their brothers when they most need them. ﴿And if they support them﴾, on assumption and supposition, ﴿they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped﴾; that is, retreat from fighting and support will surely take place from them, and they will not obtain victory from God.

{13} The reason that moved them to this is that you, O believers, ﴿are more fearful in their breasts than God﴾. They feared you more than they fear God, and preferred fear of a creature who possesses for himself and others neither benefit nor harm, over fear of the Creator in whose hand are harm, benefit, giving and withholding. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾, the ranks of matters, nor do they know the realities of things, nor do they consider consequences. Understanding in its entirety is only that the fear, hope and love of the Creator take precedence over all else, and all else follows it.

{14} ﴿They will not fight you all together﴾; that is, while they are gathered, ﴿except within fortified towns or from behind walls﴾; that is, they do not stand firm in fighting you nor resolve upon it, except when they are fortified in towns or behind walls and ramparts. For in that case, they may refuse, relying on their fortresses and walls rather than on their own courage, and this is among the greatest of censures. ﴿Their violence among themselves is severe﴾; that is, their violence among themselves is severe, with no defect in their bodies or their strength. The defect lies only in the weakness of their faith and the lack of unity of their word. For this reason He said: ﴿You think them united﴾ when you see them gathered and supporting one another, ﴿but their hearts are divided﴾; that is, mutually hateful, scattered and dispersed. ﴿That is because﴾ of what requires their attribution of what was mentioned: ﴿they are a people who do not reason﴾; that is, they have no intellect and no sound judgement. For if they had intellects, they would have preferred the superior to the inferior, and would not have accepted for themselves the basest of the two options, and their word would have been united and their hearts harmonious. Thereby they would support one another, assist one another and cooperate in their religious and worldly interests [and benefits]. Such are these forsaken People of the Book, whom God gave victory over through His Messenger, made them taste disgrace in the life of this world, and failed to support those He had promised to aid them.

{15} ﴿Like those who were before them shortly﴾: they are the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿whom Satan adorned their deeds for, and said: "No one among mankind will overcome you today, and I am your protector." But when the two armies sighted each other, he turned back on his heels and said: "I am free of you; I see what you do not see!"﴾. Their own selves deceived them, and those who deceived them, who neither benefited them nor warded off punishment from them, until they came to Badr with their pride and self-conceit, supposing that they would attain their hopes against the Messenger of God and the believers. God gave victory to His Messenger and the believers over them. They killed their leaders and chieftains, took prisoners from among them, and those who fled fled. Thereby they tasted the evil consequence of their affair and the outcome of their polytheism and transgression. This is in this world, and ﴿for them﴾ in the Hereafter is ﴿the punishment of the Fire﴾.

{16} The likeness of these hypocrites, who deceived their brothers from the People of the Book, is ﴿like the likeness of Satan when he says to man: "Disbelieve"﴾; that is, he adorned disbelief for him, made it attractive and invited him to it. When he was deceived by it, disbelieved and incurred wretchedness, the Satan who had taken charge of him and invited him to what he invited him to did not benefit him, but disowned him, ﴿and said: "Indeed I am free of you. Indeed I fear God, the Lord of the worlds."﴾; that is, I have no power to ward off the punishment from you, and I will not avail you against the weight of a speck of good.

{17} ﴿So the end of both of them﴾; that is, the caller who is Satan and the one called who is the human, when he obeyed him, ﴿is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein﴾, as God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed he calls his party only that they may be among the companions of the Blaze﴾. ﴿And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾, who shared in wrongdoing and disbelief, even if they differ in the severity and intensity of the punishment. This is the practice of Satan with all his allies: he calls them and lures them with deception to what harms them, until when they fall into the snares and the causes of ruin surround them, he disowns them and abandons them. The blame, entirely, falls upon the one who obeyed him, for God has warned against him and admonished, and informed of his aims, his ultimate purpose and his end. So the one who proceeds to obey him is a sinner with full insight, having no excuse.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 59, verse 1–17 (part 1 of 2):

It is a Medinan surah.
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent and migrated to Medina, they disbelieved in him along with the rest of the Jews who disbelieved. The Prophet (ﷺ) made a truce with the Jewish groups who were his neighbours in Medina. Then, about six months or so after the Battle of Badr, the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to them and asked them to help him pay the blood-money (diyah) for the Banu Kilab whom 'Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri had killed. They said: "We will do so, O Abu al-Qasim! Sit here until we fulfil your need!" Then some of them withdrew together, and Satan made attractive to them the wretchedness that had been decreed for them, so they conspired to kill him (ﷺ). They said: "Which of you will take this millstone, climb up and drop it on his head to crush him?" Their most wretched man, 'Amr ibn Jihash, said: "I will." They said: "You rose and we did not notice you!" He informed them of what the Jews had planned. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to them: "Leave Medina and do not live alongside me in it. I have given you a term of ten days; whoever is found after that, I will strike his neck." They stayed for some days preparing for departure. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions said "Allahu akbar" and rose against them, with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib carrying the banner. They remained in their fortresses, shooting arrows and hurling stones. Quraydah withdrew from them, and Ibn Ubayy and his allies from Ghatafan betrayed them. He agreed to let them leave with their lives and their children, and that they could take whatever their camels could carry, except weapons. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) seized the wealth and the weapons.

The property of Banu al-Nadir was exclusively for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to meet his needs and the interests of the Muslims, and he did not apply the one-fifth (khums) to it, because God had given it to him as fay' without the Muslims having to charge against it with horses or camels. He took possession of their land and homes and seized the weapons; they found fifty coats of mail, fifty helmets and three hundred and forty swords. This is the summary of their story as mentioned by the historians of the biographies (ahl al-siyar).

{1} God opens this surah by informing that everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies its Lord, declares Him free of what does not befit His majesty, worships Him and submits to His greatness, because He is the Mighty who has subdued everything, so nothing can defy Him and no difficulty is beyond Him; the Wise in His creation and command, so He creates nothing in vain and legislates nothing devoid of benefit, and does nothing except what His wisdom requires.

{2} Among that is His support of His Messenger (ﷺ) against those among the People of the Book who disbelieved, the Banu al-Nadir, when they betrayed His Messenger, so He expelled them from their homes and homelands which they had grown accustomed to and loved. Their expulsion from there was the first gathering (hashr) and exile (jala') which God had decreed against them through the hand of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), so they went to Khaybar. The noble verse indicates that they had another gathering and exile besides this; it occurred when the Prophet (ﷺ) expelled them from Khaybar, and then 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) expelled the rest of them from it. {You did not think} O Muslims {that they would go out} from their homes, because of their fortification, their strength and their honour in them, {and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah}; so they were pleased with them, were deceived by them, and reckoned that they could not be reached and no one could overcome them. But the decree of God is beyond all of that; fortresses and castles avail nothing against it, and strength and defence are of no use against it. Hence He said: {So Allah came upon them from where they did not expect}; that is, from the matter and the direction which had never occurred to them that they could be struck from, namely that He, exalted is He, {cast terror into their hearts}: and this is intense fear, which is the greatest army of Allah, against which no number, equipment, strength or might avails. The thing they counted on, and thought that a breach would enter upon them through it if it came, was the fortresses in which they had fortified themselves and in which their souls were at rest.
